solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bad headache from one rye, perhaps, consumed by me

indicators.note: being consumed by something means being swallowed up inside it, so these pieces go within the word me

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
rye is an example of a cereal grain, as the 'perhaps' signals

explanation.surface: Someone blames a whisky or a loaf of rye bread they ate for their pounding head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rye, perhaps' looks like the cause of the headache, but it is a definition by example of GRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe, often one-sided recurring headache is a classic migraine; it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Millions request protective cover

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A huge number of people ask for something to shield them, as in a pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: A face covering worn for safety, such as a surgical one, is a protective cover.

clue.text: Fan glad to be disguised as Tolkien's wizard

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the letters of the two words are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A happy fan dresses up as a famous fantasy wizard, perhaps at a convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey, later white, wizard of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings is J.R.R. Tolkien's best-known magician.

clue.text: Concept of muscle's pulling power

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles; the 's reads as 'muscles'
traction is the power of pulling a load

explanation.surface: A question about the idea behind a muscle's ability to pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concept of' looks like part of a physics phrase, but 'Concept' alone is the definition and 'of' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract idea, as opposed to a concrete thing, is a concept: the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: What thin and tasteless wine has? Not one

definitions.text: What thin and tasteless wine has
definitions.meaning: wine tasters call a full, weighty wine one with body; a thin, tasteless one has none of it

explanation.surface: A wine critic dismisses a weak vintage, then says nobody likes it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words, NO BODY, describing a weak wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a single person is the plain everyday sense of the pronoun; the first sense is the wine taster's term split in two.

clue.text: Go up, cutting first bit off branch of tree

indicators.note: removing the first bit means the opening letter of the word for 'go up' is dropped

parts.note: to climb is to go up

explanation.surface: Instructions to someone who climbs a tree and saws off a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting first bit off' removes the C from CLIMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A large main bough of a tree is called a limb, the same word as for an arm or leg.

clue.text: Angry buccaneer denied power

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so the letter for power is removed

parts.note: a buccaneer is a pirate
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A pirate captain is furious at losing his grip on authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and cross are the everyday synonyms; irate is simply a formal word for angry.

clue.text: Unusual three-bar interval

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary arrangement, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician remarks on an odd rest lasting three bars in a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-bar interval' reads as a musical rest, but the hyphenated word is the fodder and 'interval' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause or break to rest, such as a rest during work or exercise, is a breather.

clue.text: Cavity made with spades in United States

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Someone digs a hole with spades somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a placement instruction, but it gives its own letters, IN, as a piece of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow space in bone, especially the air-filled spaces in the skull behind the nose, is a sinus.

clue.text: Sustained attack of anger in pub?

parts.note: a bar is a pub, or the counter in one
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Asking whether a long verbal assault is just the fury found in a drinking house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger in pub' reads cryptically as 'bar rage', on the model of road rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolonged artillery bombardment, or a relentless stream of criticism, is a barrage.

clue.text: Again found cooked beast covered in sauce

indicators.note: covered in sauce means wrapped by it, so the sauce word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a relish is a piquant sauce or condiment

indicators.note: cooked suggests the raw letters of beast are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the cooked animal has been smothered in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning to set up or establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something again means to set it up anew; found is the verb meaning establish, and the prefix means again.

clue.text: Cutting short drab meeting that's out of control

indicators.note: letters out of control are in disorder, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants to end a dull meeting that has descended into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortening a text or speech is an abridgement; the noun names the act of cutting it down.

clue.text: Rally partner with fish taken on Thames?

indicators.note: in a down clue the fish is placed on top of the next piece, so it comes first

parts.note: the cod is a fish
the Thames is a river, the one flowing through London

explanation.surface: A boating partner brings a fish aboard on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' suggests a political gathering, but it is motor rallying, where a navigator sits beside the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor rallying the navigator who reads pace notes beside the driver is a co-driver, the driver's partner.

clue.text: No longer chilling in working environment

parts.note: something off is no longer happening, as when an event is called off
ice chills things down, so it stands for chilling

explanation.surface: A worker says they no longer relax at their workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilling' suggests relaxing, but it is used in its cooling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where desk work is done, a workplace, is an office.

clue.text: Page held by old and overused fastener

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside it, so the letter for page goes within

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh, or hackneyed

explanation.surface: A sheet of paper is clipped by a worn-out old fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire clip driven through paper to fix sheets together is a staple, a kind of fastener.

clue.text: Trailer parking needs formal assessment

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a review is a formal assessment, as of a policy or performance

explanation.surface: Parking a caravan requires an official inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a towed vehicle, but here it is a film trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short advance showing of a film, a trailer, is a preview of it.

clue.text: A change involving island enclosure for birds

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the island letter goes inside the word for change

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: An alteration to a bird enclosure on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cage or building in which birds are kept, as at a zoo, is an aviary.

clue.text: Lie with vertebra broken — one may get back something like this?

definitions.text: one may get back something like this

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lying down with a broken vertebra, someone hopes their back can be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back' plays on the spine: the surface is about an injured back, while the definition means recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be recovered or got back is retrievable; the adjective describes such a thing.

clue.text: Bound round run getting exhausted

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the word for bound encloses the letter for run

parts.note: bound means tied up
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jogger tethered while running in circles becomes worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out and weary, needing rest, is the sense of tired, a direct synonym of exhausted.

clue.text: Unsightly inner core of Bruges gets left years

indicators.note: the inner core of a word is its central letters, here the middle two

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year(s)

explanation.surface: The centre of the Belgian city of Bruges is said to have grown ugly over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant to look at is the plain meaning of both words: a straight synonym.

clue.text: What's partly over and above porch

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A question asking what lies partly above a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed platform along the outside of a house is a veranda; a porch is a similar covered entrance.

clue.text: Don't start cutting up top layer of wedding cake

indicators.note: not starting means losing the opening letter of the word for cutting up

parts.note: dicing is cutting food up into small cubes

explanation.surface: A warning not to begin slicing the top tier of a wedding cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the D from DICING.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar coating spread over a cake, such as the hard white coating on a wedding cake, is icing.

clue.text: Regret accommodating daughter that's insolent

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the letter for daughter goes inside the word for regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A parent regrets putting up with a daughter who is cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite and disrespectful, cheeky, is the sense shared by rude and insolent.

clue.text: Article found in minor road in passing

indicators.note: being found in something means lying inside it, so the article goes within the word for minor road

parts.note: a byway is a minor road
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article turns up on a quiet side road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In passing' sounds like part of the road scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioned incidentally, as an aside, is the idiom: said in passing.
